---
name: subagents
description: How the Horizon agent delegates to native subagents for review and upkeep — spawning by name, read-only enforcement, dispatch-time model choice, and the dynamic descriptor roster.
---

Subagents are **your team's workers**: focused helpers you (the team lead) spawn
to divide up review and upkeep while you keep proving. This is delegation
*within* your team and needs no permission — distinct from launching new tasks or
runs for *other* teams, which is off by default (see the `horizon` skill,
"Delegating beyond your team"). The `ground` helper is the fresh-context
checkpoint for workspace-wide strategy and hygiene; it is a subagent, not a
second orchestrator role.

Bundled descriptors and any workspace overrides under
`.archon-horizon/subagents/<name>.md` are merged at the start of every `horizon
run`, then compiled into your engine's **native** subagent format,
workspace-local:

- Claude Code → `.claude/agents/<name>.md`
- Codex → `.codex/agents/<name>.toml`

Use the engine's native roster, or list `.codex/agents/*.toml` for Codex and
`.claude/agents/*.md` for Claude, to see every runnable helper. Do not treat an
empty `.archon-horizon/subagents/` directory as an empty roster: that directory
holds workspace overrides/custom helpers only; built-ins such as `ground`,
`janitor`, and `work-reviewer` still appear in the compiled native directory.
Pick the right helper and scope from those generated descriptions.

## Dispatch

Spawn a subagent **by name** through your engine's own native subagent
mechanism, with a focused directive: the slice/scope (a chapter, a task, a
project) and the project it applies to. Spawn several in parallel when the work
divides cleanly, then wait for and reconcile their reports. Give one subagent
one scoped slice so the workspace scales to many projects.

Delegation is part of the normal workflow, not an exceptional recovery path.
For a session that touches more than one file, more than one proof obligation,
or is expected to run longer than ten minutes, dispatch at least one bounded
review/helper before the final report. On a multi-session task, dispatch
`ground` before the terminal completion claim and `janitor` at the scheduled
hygiene checkpoints. Use the engine's native `spawn_agent`/Task mechanism,
wait for the helper to finish, and reconcile its report in your own result. If
no suitable helper is available, state why delegation was skipped in the report.

## Read-only and write scope

A descriptor's `read_only: true` is compiled to real engine enforcement — Claude
`disallowedTools: [Edit, Write, NotebookEdit]`, Codex `sandbox_mode = "read-only"`
— so a read-only reviewer cannot edit source. Every subagent (read-only or not)
can still file issues/memory and write its report via the `horizon inbox` CLI;
that is how read-only agents act. The descriptor's `write_domain` documents what
a writer is expected to touch (Lean/blueprint/reference source).

## Model and effort — the Horizon agent owns the spend

Descriptors intentionally carry no model, tier, or effort setting. Generated
Claude/Codex descriptors inherit the parent session by default. At dispatch time,
the Horizon agent chooses the native model and reasoning effort for that helper:
use the same model/effort for mathematical review, a lighter capable option for
mechanical search/lint/hygiene, and a vision-capable option for page transcription.
If the engine cannot express a per-call override, inherit the parent and record
the choice in the report rather than hiding a model policy in `config.yaml`.

The same rule applies to a named subagent, a bare Task/Agent spawn, or any
workflow fan-out. Match model and effort to the actual slice, and before a large
fan-out check `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. If headroom is low, commit work in
flight first so an interruption loses nothing.

To add or change a subagent, edit its descriptor under
`.archon-horizon/subagents/` — it recompiles on the next run. Do not rely on a
stale hard-coded roster in this skill.

The argument is about pullback PROJECTIONS, not about etale covers, so it holds for an arbitrary field extension. Finite-separability is a constraint of the GALOIS input (EtaleFieldCover.lean, input 1) and was double-counted onto this brick.

(1) Total-space cancellation: one mathlib lemma, pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso -- baseChangeField C k-prime IS by definition the pullback of C.hom along phi, so C_k-prime x_k-prime T and C x_k T are canonically isomorphic. (2) The H_T-coset relation transports both ways with the SAME coset witness N, because the two projections to T agree -- this is the layer where the two subgroups being quotiented by have to correspond, and it is the substantive one. (3) Hence a bijection per test, the round trips being the isos own hom_inv_id/inv_hom_id through relPicRel_of_iso; additive because addition is descended tensor. (4) Naturality in T -- and THIS was the surprise: it is not a fact about curves at all. Stated for an ARBITRARY category with pullbacks (pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso_naturality) it falls to pullback.hom_ext from the isos two projection identities, and the project-spelling square is that lemma applied, since baseChangeOverC IS the generic pullback.map.

Restriction along Over.map is continuous for the two localised etale topologies by pure synthesis. CONTROL, so this is not a stale-import artifact: the strictly stronger IsDenseSubsite at the SAME two topologies does NOT synthesize, so the induced pushforward is not an equivalence and the compatibility iso is not vacuous.

    "kind": "memory",
    "author": "horizon",
    "body": "A "TRAP, MEASURED -- DO NOT ROUTE VIA X" NOTE IS THE HIGHEST-LEVERAGE FALSE CLAIM A LANE CAN SHIP, AND THE CHEAPEST TEST IS TO GREP WHETHER A SIBLING FILE ALREADY DOES X.

WHAT HAPPENED (AJCR, pic-c 0092 r5, Pic0VanishingFieldGenusZero.lean:33-38). A lane recorded, in a file header, a commit message, and a direct message to another lane: "going through chi_moduleKSheaf at baseChangeBundle C K produces the same object under a different Over instance, and the two chi terms DO NOT UNIFY -- measured". It reads like exactly the kind of hard-won spelling fact worth broadcasting, and the receiving lane accepted it.

It is false. The bundled route closes with one `change` to the bundled spelling followed by `simpa`, at DEFAULT heartbeats. What had been measured was that one `simpa` failed without the `change`, i.e. a fact about a tactic invocation, published as a fact about two objects.

THE TEST THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT COST ONE GREP. A sibling lane had written the prohibited proof, at a concrete curve, in the same hour, and it was at HEAD and root-imported: Curve/P1DegreeZeroTrivial.lean:83-99 uses chi_moduleKSheaf at baseChangeBundle with the same change + simpa. So before publishing "route X does not work", grep the tree for X: a live use site refutes the prohibition outright, and its presence in a file you did not write is more likely than it feels, because a prohibition is usually discovered exactly when two lanes are on the same object.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN AN ORDINARY OVERCLAIM. A positive overclaim gets tested when someone tries to use the result. A prohibition is never tested -- its whole function is to stop people trying -- so it can survive indefinitely and it forecloses a cheap route for every later round. /-!
# FGA representability of the Picard scheme

This file states the FGA representability of the relative Picard functor of a
smooth proper geometrically integral curve `C/k`, following Kleiman, "The
Picard scheme", §2 and §4 (cf. FGA Explained Ch. 9; arXiv:math/0504020).

The relative Picard functor is

```
picSharp C := PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat
```

the set-valued shadow of the `H_T`-coset carrier
`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` of `Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` (Kleiman §2
Def. `df:Pfs`; blueprint `def:rel_pic_sharp`). A `RepresentableBy` witness
against it is a natural bijection
`(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`, which is what the downstream
tangent-space computation (`AJC.pic0av`, `Pic0.tangentSpaceIso`) attaches to.

## The étale-sheafification route (owner decision of 2026-07-28)

Kleiman §4 represents the **étale-sheafified** functor `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, and
that is what this file's obligation is stated against —
`fgaPicardRepresentability`, over an **arbitrary** base field, with **no
hypothesis on `C(k)`**. The functor is built and its sheaf property proved in
`Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean` (`PicScheme.picEt`, `picEt_isSheaf_forget`), by
sheafifying the relative Picard presheaf for Mathlib's big étale topology
localised at `Spec k`.

Why the sheafification is not optional. The plain relative functor
`picSharp C = T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` is not representable over a
general field, so an unconditional `RepresentableBy` against `picSharp` is a
**false** statement, not merely an unproved one.

**CITATION CORRECTED 2026-07-29 (`review-ajc`), by reading the source. The
conclusion above is right; the reason previously given for it was not.** This
paragraph used to say `picSharp` "is not even a Zariski sheaf (Kleiman §2
L1292–L1302)". Those lines
(`references/kleiman-picard-src/kleiman-picard.tex`, the full paper) say
something else: "The **absolute** Picard functor `Pic_X` is never a separated
presheaf in the Zariski topology", proved with the `ℙ¹_X`/`O(1)` argument. That
is about `Pic_X`, **not** about the relative `Pic_{X/S} = picSharp`, which is
*defined* by quotienting out `Pic(T)` precisely to defeat that argument. What
Kleiman actually asserts about the relative functor is weaker (L1330): "Since
`Pic_{X/S}` is not *a priori* a sheaf, it is remarkable that it is representable
so often in practice." Not-a-priori is not never — indeed L1600–L1605 proves
`Pic_{X/S} ≅ Pic_{(X/S)zar}` whenever `f` has a section.

**The witness, and it satisfies exactly this file's binders.** Kleiman
L5105–L5108 (repeated L5126–L5129): take `X : u² + v² + w² = 0` in `ℙ²_ℝ`, a
smooth plane conic — hence smooth, proper, and geometrically integral, since
`X_ℂ ≅ ℙ¹_ℂ` — over a field where it has **no** rational point. `Pic_{(X/ℝ)ét}`
is representable by §4 `th:main`, the two functors differ (Exercise `ex:Pfs`),
and Kleiman concludes `Pic_{X/ℝ}` is not representable.

**That last step is now a Lean theorem rather than a quotation**, which is the
right state for something this load-bearing:
`PicScheme.not_exists_representing_picSharp_of_not_isIso`
(`Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean`, `ajc-p1`) derives *from* `¬ IsIso
(picEtComparison C)` that **no** scheme represents `picSharp C` — the existential
of clause (1), not merely the pinned `PicScheme C`. No topology and no sheaf step
enter. So the falsity of the `picSharp` analogue of clause (1) is reduced to the
single residue that the comparison really does fail for that conic (via
`φ^* O(1)` and `h⁰` on `ℙ¹_ℂ`), which is where Kleiman's own argument lives and
is not yet formalised.

**Do not route this through a Zariski-sheaf claim** (corrected again the same
day, after `work-reviewer` refuted the first repair — see `I-0970`). It is
tempting to argue "representable ⟹ Zariski sheaf, and `picSharp` is not one";
the second half is *not* what the sources say. `ex:Pfs` compares
`Pic_{(X/ℝ)zar}` with `Pic_{(X/ℝ)ét}` — both already sheaves — so it witnesses
`zar ≠ ét`, not a failure of Zariski descent for the unsheafified functor. And
Kleiman `th:cmp` part 1 (L1391–L1393) proves `Pic_{X/S} ↪ Pic_{(X/S)zar}`
whenever `O_S ≅ f_* O_X` holds universally, which is automatic on these binders —
i.e. `picSharp` *is* Zariski-separated here, and any failure could only be
gluing. The non-representability above needs no sheaf step at all, so take it
directly. Kleiman §2 **Thm 2.5** repairs it only under a
**section**: given one (and `O_S = f_* O_X` universally, automatic for our
proper geometrically integral `C/k`), the comparisons

```
Pic_{X/S}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)ét}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)fppf}(T)
```

are bijective. That conditional route survives here as
`picEtComparison_isIso_of_hasRationalPoint` and `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint`,
both clearly labelled as **strictly weaker than the challenge**. They are not
the headline and must not be reported as progress toward it. (Earlier revisions
of this file named a class `PicEtComparisonIso` in these four places; no such
declaration exists or ever landed — the comparison is supplied by the theorem
`picEtComparison_isIso_of_hasRationalPoint`, which is clause (2) of
`fgaPicardRepresentability` applied to the section. Corrected 2026-07-29.)

The two interfaces, and which one to build against:

* `HasPicSchemeEt` / `PicSchemeEt` / `representableEt` / `groupSchemeStructureEt`
  — **unconditional**, the étale formulation, the target. New work goes here.
* `HasPicScheme` / `PicScheme` / `representable` / `groupSchemeStructure` — the
  legacy `picSharp`-shaped interface, whose only producer is now the
  conditional `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint`. Consumers quantifying over
  `[HasPicScheme C]` as a hypothesis remain valid and kernel-clean; they are
  simply conditional statements until restated against `picEt`.

  point. The file's only `sorry`.

    11	/-!
    12	# Quasi-projectivity, as the vocabulary `FiniteInAffine` was standing in for
    13	
    14	`Scheme.FiniteInAffine X` (`Picard/PicEtPointedReduction.lean`) says every finite
    15	subset of `X` lies in a single affine open.  It is the elementary, action-free form
    16	of the EGA II 4.5.4 hypothesis that the whole finite-Galois-quotient engine runs
    17	on, and up to now the project carried it **by hand**, with the same sentence
    18	written in three places: *"it holds for quasi-projective `X`, but mathlib has no
    19	quasi-projectivity vocabulary at this pin, so for the curve it must be supplied by
    20	hand"* (`Picard/PicEtPointedReduction.lean`,
    21	`Albanese/StableAffineCoverGroup.lean`, `Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`).
    22	
    23	This file removes the hand: it derives `FiniteInAffine` **from projectivity**, for
    24	the project's own `Scheme.Hom.IsProjective`.  The chain is
    25	
    26	  graded prime avoidance  ⟹  `FiniteInAffine (Proj 𝒜)`
    27	                          ⟹  `FiniteInAffine ℙ(n; S)`   (affine morphism descent)
    28	                          ⟹  `FiniteInAffine X` for `X` projective over `S`.
    29	
    30	## What was actually missing, and it is one lemma
    31	
    32	Of those three steps only the first has content, and it is **absent from mathlib
    33	`v4.31`**: there is no *graded* prime avoidance.  Mathlib has
    34	`Ideal.subset_union_prime_finite` — a homogeneous ideal not contained in the union
    35	of finitely many primes is not contained in any one of them — but the element it
    36	produces is an arbitrary element of the ideal, while
    37	`AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.isAffineOpen_basicOpen` demands `f ∈ 𝒜 m` with `0 < m`.
    38	Getting a **homogeneous** avoiding element of **positive degree** is §1, and it is
    39	where the grading is consumed.
    40	
    41	The two descent steps are cheap and they are cheap for a reason worth recording:
    42	`IsClosedImmersion → IsAffineHom` is a mathlib instance, and `IsAffineOpen.preimage`
    43	turns an affine open of the target into an affine open of the source.  So
    44	`FiniteInAffine` propagates **down** every affine morphism
    45	(`Scheme.finiteInAffine_of_isAffineHom`), and a closed immersion into `ℙ(n; S)` is
    46	one.  This is the same shape as the already-landed
    47	`Scheme.finiteInAffine_left_of_isAffineHom`, generalised off the relative setting.
    48	
    49	## What this does and does not buy
    50	
    51	It does **not** discharge the `FiniteInAffine` conjunct of
    52	`Scheme.PointedPicSharpRep`.  That conjunct is about the **Picard scheme**, and
    53	nothing in this project produces projectivity of a Picard scheme — that is
    54	Kleiman §5 `th:qpp&p`, an open obligation.  What changes is the *kind* of thing
    55	that is open: the antecedent's last non-projection conjunct is now reducible to a
    56	standard geometric hypothesis with a standard proof, rather than an elementary
    57	condition invented here.  Stated as `Scheme.finiteInAffine_of_isProjective` in §3.
    58	
    59	It **does** discharge, unconditionally and for free, the orbit hypothesis of the
    60	Galois-descent engine at every projective scheme
    61	(`Scheme.orbitsInAffineOpen_of_isProjective`), which is what
    62	`Picard/GaloisQuotientNonVacuity.lean` had only for *affine* `X` and what the
    63	Albanese lane's `OrbitsInAffineOpen` had for no `X` at all.  Smooth proper
    64	geometrically integral curves **are** projective in this project
    65	(`AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.isProjective_of_smoothProperGeometricallyIntegral`,
    66	`Picard/CurveProjectivity.lean`), so §3 fires at the curve itself with no
    67	hypothesis beyond its own binders.
    68	
    69	## What §5 is NOT: read this before consuming `PointedPicSharpRepProjective`
    70	
    71	§5 restates the seam's antecedent with `IsProjective` of the representing scheme in
    72	place of `FiniteInAffine`.  **That antecedent is refuted at the object it is about**,
    73	and the refutation is landed here as a theorem, not left as prose:
    74	`Scheme.not_isProjective_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover`.  Projectivity over a field
    75	forces `IsProper`, hence `UniversallyClosed`, hence — over the compact `Spec k` —
    76	`CompactSpace` (`Scheme.compactSpace_of_isProjective`); and the full Picard scheme is a
    77	**disjoint union over `deg ∈ ℤ`** (Kleiman §4 `th:main`(1)), which is not quasi-compact.
    78	So `PointedPicSharpRepProjective` is not the standard hypothesis restated — it is
    79	strictly stronger and false at `Pic_{C/k}`.
    80	
    81	This is verbatim the trap `Picard/AmbientPicNotProper.lean` exists to record, "trap (c):
    82	a `P → Q` whose antecedent is unsatisfiable in the intended setting", and it is caught by
    83	that file's own theorems.  Kleiman's `th:qpp&p` gives quasi-projectivity of the **degree
    84	pieces**, not projectivity of the ambient scheme.  §5 therefore survives only as a
    85	*conditional* reduction with an explicitly refuted antecedent; §3 and §4, which do not
    86	mention the ambient Picard scheme, are unaffected.
    87	
    88	An earlier revision of this section said §5 states the seam "with no condition invented
    89	in this project anywhere in it".  Both halves were wrong: `Scheme.Hom.IsProjective` is
    90	project-local (`Picard/ProjectiveMorphismBasic.lean`, mathlib `v4.31` has no
    91	morphism-level projectivity at all), as are `PicScheme.picSharp` and
    92	`Scheme.HasRationalPoint`; and the antecedent is not merely non-standard but refutable.
    93	The defensible statement is the narrow one: the *mathematical notion* is standard even
    94	though the Lean definition is ours.
    95	
    96	## Non-vacuity
    97	
    98	`FiniteInAffine` is satisfiable at an affine scheme with `⊤`
    99	(`Scheme.finiteInAffine_of_isAffine`, already landed) and that witness is
   100	*degenerate*: it says nothing about the projective case.  So the honest
   101	non-degeneracy evidence for §2 is what a fresh-context audit could **verify**, and it
   102	is at `Proj`: `Proj (homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) ℚ)` is nonempty (the point
   103	`V(X₀)`), and the hypotheses of `Scheme.exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_notMem` are jointly
   104	satisfiable there, both checked by elaborating them at that named object.
   105	
   106	**What is NOT verified, stated because an earlier revision of this paragraph asserted
   107	it as the ground of non-degeneracy:** that `ℙ(n; S)` fails to be affine for `n` with at
   108	least two elements.  It is true, but it is proved nowhere in mathlib at this pin
   109	(no `¬ IsAffine` results at all) nor in this project, so
   110	`Scheme.finiteInAffine_projectiveSpace` being a *non-affine* witness rests on prose.
   111	That earlier revision also claimed the caution "is recorded as
   112	`Scheme.finiteInAffine_projectiveSpace`"; that theorem records no such thing — it has no
   113	`Nonempty` hypothesis and no non-affineness content.
   114	-/

    14	
    15	A finite morphism to the projective line supplies finite Laurent two-chart
    16	data, hence a closed immersion into a relative projective space.  The existing
    17	nonconstant-map construction produces that finite morphism under exactly the

    33	/-- A proper scheme admitting a finite morphism to the projective line is
    34	projective over the base field. -/
    35	theorem isProjective_of_hasFiniteMapToP1
    36	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    37	    [IsProper C.hom] [HasFiniteMapToP1 C] : C.hom.IsProjective := by
    38	  obtain ⟨pi, hpi⟩ := HasFiniteMapToP1.nonempty_finite_map (C := C)
    39	  letI : IsFinite pi.left := hpi
    40	  exact (p1LaurentChartData k).isProjective_of_finiteMap pi
    41	
    42	/-- A smooth proper geometrically integral relative curve is projective over
    43	the base field. -/
    44	theorem isProjective_of_smoothProperGeometricallyIntegral
    45	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    46	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    47	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] : C.hom.IsProjective := by
    48	  haveI : HasFiniteMapToP1 C := inferInstance
    49	  exact isProjective_of_hasFiniteMapToP1 C

    51	/-- At the scheme universe supported by `IsProjectiveWith`, a smooth proper
    52	geometrically integral relative curve carries a relatively very ample line
    53	bundle, with no hypothesis beyond the curve's own. -/
    54	theorem exists_isProjectiveWith_of_smoothProperGeometricallyIntegral
    55	    {k₀ : Type} [Field k₀] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k₀)))
    56	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    57	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] :
    58	    ∃ L : C.left.Modules, C.hom.IsProjectiveWith L :=
    59	  (isProjective_of_smoothProperGeometricallyIntegral C).exists_isProjectiveWith

    61	/-- Projectivity under exactly the smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible
    62	curve hypotheses used by the algebraic Jacobian challenge. -/
    63	theorem isProjective_of_smoothProperGeometricallyIrreducible
    64	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    65	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    66	    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] : C.hom.IsProjective := by
    67	  letI : GeometricallyIntegral C.hom :=
    68	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension.geometricallyIntegral 1 C.hom

    74	theorem exists_isProjectiveWith_of_smoothProperGeometricallyIrreducible

   414	
   415	/-- **A scheme projective over an affine base satisfies `FiniteInAffine`.**
   416	
   417	This is the statement three files in this project asserted in prose and none proved.
   418	`Scheme.Hom.IsProjective` (`Picard/ProjectiveMorphismBasic.lean`) unfolds to a closed

   708	
   709	/-- **`FiniteInAffine` is closed under arbitrary set-indexed coproducts.**  If every
   710	component scheme `g i` satisfies `FiniteInAffine`, so does `∐ g`.
   711	
   712	A finite `s ⊆ ∐ g` meets only the finitely many components indexed by `idx '' s`; within
   713	each, `s` pulls back along the open immersion `Sigma.ι g i` to a finite set covered by an
   714	affine open `U i`; the images `Sigma.ι g i ''ᵁ U i` are pairwise disjoint
   715	(`disjoint_opensRange_sigmaι`) affine opens (image of an affine open under an open
   716	immersion), so their finite `iSup` is affine (`IsAffineOpen.biSup_of_disjoint`) and
   717	contains `s`.
   718	
   719	This is the property `§5.5`'s refutation identified as the one the degree-graded Picard
   720	scheme has and global projectivity does not. -/
   721	theorem finiteInAffine_sigma {σ : Type v} [Small.{u, v} σ] (g : σ → Scheme.{u})
   722	    (h : ∀ i, FiniteInAffine (g i)) : FiniteInAffine (∐ g) := by
   723	  classical
   724	  letI : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion (Sigma.ι g i) := fun i =>
   725	    Scheme.IsLocallyDirected.instIsOpenImmersionι (Discrete.functor g) { as := i }
   726	  intro s hs
   727	  have hcomp : ∀ x : (∐ g : Scheme.{u}), ∃ i, x ∈ Set.range (Sigma.ι g i).base := by
   728	    intro x
   729	    obtain ⟨i, y, hy⟩ := (sigmaOpenCover g).exists_eq x
   730	    exact ⟨i, y, hy⟩
   731	  choose idx hidx using hcomp
   732	  have hpre : ∀ i : σ, ((Sigma.ι g i).base ⁻¹' s).Finite := fun i =>
   733	    hs.preimage ((Sigma.ι g i).isOpenEmbedding.injective).injOn
   734	  choose U hU using fun i => h i _ (hpre i)
   735	  set J : Set σ := idx '' s with hJ
   736	  have hJfin : J.Finite := hs.image idx
   737	  refine ⟨⟨⨆ i ∈ J, (Sigma.ι g i) ''ᵁ (U i).1, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
   738	  · apply IsAffineOpen.biSup_of_disjoint hJfin
   739	    · intro i _
   740	      exact (U i).2.image_of_isOpenImmersion _
   741	    · intro i _ j _ hij
   742	      exact Disjoint.mono (Scheme.Hom.image_le_opensRange _ _)
   743	        (Scheme.Hom.image_le_opensRange _ _) (disjoint_opensRange_sigmaι g i j hij)
   744	  · intro x hx
   745	    obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := hidx x
   746	    have hyU : y ∈ (U (idx x)).1 := by
   747	      apply hU (idx x)
   748	      simp only [Set.mem_preimage, hy]
   749	      exact hx
   750	    have hmem : x ∈ (Sigma.ι g (idx x)) ''ᵁ (U (idx x)).1 := ⟨y, hyU, hy⟩
   751	    exact (le_iSup₂ (f := fun i _ => (Sigma.ι g i) ''ᵁ (U i).1) (idx x)
   752	      ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩) hmem
   753	
   754	/-- **`FiniteInAffine` is closed under binary coproducts.**  The two-piece case of
   755	`finiteInAffine_sigma`, via `coprodIsoSigma` and the landed
   756	`Scheme.finiteInAffine_of_iso` (`Picard/PicEtPointedReduction.lean`). -/
   757	theorem finiteInAffine_coprod {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (hX : FiniteInAffine X)
   758	    (hY : FiniteInAffine Y) : FiniteInAffine (X ⨿ Y) := by
   759	  refine finiteInAffine_of_iso (coprodIsoSigma X Y).symm ?_
   760	  apply finiteInAffine_sigma
   761	  rintro ⟨i⟩
   762	  cases i
   763	  · simpa using hX
   764	  · simpa using hY
   765	
   766	end Coproduct

    11	/-!
    12	# Projective morphisms carrying a very ample line bundle
    13	
    14	Mathlib v4.31 has no projective-morphism class and no (very) ampleness
    15	vocabulary.  Following the encoding settled in inbox `I-0118` (comment
    16	`C-0002`), this file defines:
    17	
    18	* `ProjectiveSpace.twistingSheaf n₀ S m` — the Serre twist `O(m)` on the
    19	  relative projective space `ℙ(n₀; S)`, the pullback of
    20	  `ProjTwist.serreTwist` from the integral model along `toProjInt`;
    21	* `ProjectiveSpace.twistingSheafBaseChange` — `O(m)` commutes with base
    22	  change of the ambient projective space;
    23	* `Scheme.Hom.IsProjectiveWith π L` — the **projective-with-`L`** predicate:
    24	  `π : X ⟶ S` factors through a closed immersion `i : X ↪ ℙ(n; S)` for a
    25	  finite coordinate type `n`, over `S` with `L ≅ i^* O(1)`;
    26	
    27	with the stability facts the Quot-scheme endgame consumes:
    28	
    29	* `Scheme.Hom.IsProjectiveWith.isProper` — projective morphisms are proper;
    30	* `Scheme.Hom.IsProjectiveWith.comp_isClosedImmersion` — a closed immersion
    31	  into a projective scheme is projective (carrying the restricted bundle);
    32	* `Scheme.Hom.IsProjectiveWith.baseChange` — stability under base change
    33	  (carrying the pulled-back bundle).
    34	
    35	Everything is at `Scheme.{0}`: the Serre twist rests on the descent engine
    36	`Scheme.Modules.glue`, which is universe-monomorphic at `Scheme.GlueData.{0}`
    37	(`GlueDescent.lean:934`).
    38	
    39	Blueprint: `def:twisting_sheaf`, `def:projective_with`,
    40	`lem:projective_with_proper`, `lem:projective_with_closed_immersion`,
    41	`lem:projective_with_base_change`
    42	(`blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_QuotScheme.tex`).
    43	-/
    44	
    45	open CategoryTheory Limits MvPolynomial
    46	
    47	noncomputable section
    48	
    49	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    50	
    51	namespace ProjectiveSpace
    52	
    53	variable (n₀ : Type) (S : Scheme.{0})
    54	
    55	/-- The Serre twist `O(m)` on the relative projective space `ℙ(n₀; S)`:
    56	the pullback of the glued twisting sheaf on the integral model. -/
    57	def twistingSheaf (m : ℕ) : (ℙ(n₀; S)).Modules :=
    58	  (Scheme.Modules.pullback (toProjInt n₀ S)).obj (ProjTwist.serreTwist n₀ m)
    59	
    60	variable {S} {S' : Scheme.{0}}
    61	
    62	/-- The Serre twist commutes with base change of the ambient projective
    63	space: `(map g)^* O(m) ≅ O(m)`. -/
    64	def twistingSheafBaseChange (g : S' ⟶ S) (m : ℕ) :
    65	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback (map n₀ g)).obj (twistingSheaf n₀ S m) ≅
    66	      twistingSheaf n₀ S' m :=
    67	  Scheme.pullbackTriangleIso (map_toProjInt n₀ g) (ProjTwist.serreTwist n₀ m)
    68	
    69	end ProjectiveSpace
    70	
    71	/-- `π : X ⟶ S` is a **projective morphism carrying the line bundle `L`**
    72	([Nitsure] §5, [EGA II] 5.5): there are a finite coordinate type `n`, a closed
    73	immersion `i : X ↪ ℙ(n; S)` over `S`, and an isomorphism of `L` with the
    74	pullback of the Serre twist `O(1)`.  This is the faithful encoding of
    75	"projective with relatively very ample `L`" settled in inbox `I-0118`. -/
    76	def Scheme.Hom.IsProjectiveWith {X S : Scheme.{0}} (π : X ⟶ S) (L : X.Modules) :
    77	    Prop :=
    78	  ∃ (n : Type) (_ : Finite n) (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)),
    79	    IsClosedImmersion i ∧ i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = π ∧
    80	      Nonempty (L ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj
    81	        (ProjectiveSpace.twistingSheaf n S 1))
    82	
    83	namespace Scheme.Hom.IsProjective
    84	
    85	variable {X S : Scheme.{0}} {π : X ⟶ S}
    86	
    87	/-- Every projective morphism carries a relatively very ample line bundle: choose the
    88	pullback of `O(1)` along the closed immersion in the `IsProjective` witness. -/
    89	theorem exists_isProjectiveWith (h : π.IsProjective) :
    90	    ∃ L : X.Modules, π.IsProjectiveWith L := by
    91	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
    92	  letI : Finite n := hn
    93	  let L := (Scheme.Modules.pullback i).obj
    94	    (ProjectiveSpace.twistingSheaf n S 1)
    95	  exact ⟨L, n, inferInstance, i, hi, hcomp, ⟨Iso.refl _⟩⟩
    96	
    97	end Scheme.Hom.IsProjective
    98	
    99	namespace Scheme.Hom.IsProjectiveWith
   100	
   101	variable {X S : Scheme.{0}} {π : X ⟶ S} {L : X.Modules}
   102	
   103	/-- Forget the chosen very ample line bundle from a projective morphism. -/
   104	theorem isProjective (h : π.IsProjectiveWith L) : π.IsProjective := by
   105	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp, -⟩ := h
   106	  exact ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩
   107	
   108	/-- **Projective morphisms are proper**: a closed immersion is proper, the
   109	structural morphism of projective space is proper, and properness is stable
   110	under composition. -/
   111	theorem isProper (h : π.IsProjectiveWith L) : IsProper π := by
   112	  exact h.isProjective.isProper
   113	
   114	/-- **Projective morphisms are locally of finite type**: immediate from
   115	`isProper`, since properness extends `LocallyOfFiniteType`.  This lets the
   116	Quot-scheme endgame and the Hilbert-polynomial existence theorem derive finite
   117	type from projectivity instead of carrying it as a separate hypothesis. -/
   118	theorem locallyOfFiniteType (h : π.IsProjectiveWith L) : LocallyOfFiniteType π :=
   119	  haveI := h.isProper; inferInstance
   120	
   121	/-- **Projective morphisms are separated** (properness extends `IsSeparated`). -/
   122	theorem isSeparated (h : π.IsProjectiveWith L) : IsSeparated π :=
   123	  haveI := h.isProper; inferInstance
   124	
   125	/-- **Projective morphisms are universally closed** (properness extends
   126	`UniversallyClosed`). -/
   127	theorem universallyClosed (h : π.IsProjectiveWith L) : UniversallyClosed π :=
   128	  haveI := h.isProper; inferInstance
   129	
   130	/-- **Transfer along an isomorphism of the carried bundle**: `IsProjectiveWith`
   131	depends on `L` only up to isomorphism (it records the comparison `L ≅ i^* O(1)`
   132	through `Nonempty`), so if `π` is projective carrying `L` and `L ≅ L'`, then `π`
   133	is projective carrying `L'`.  Useful for consumers that only have the bundle up
   134	to isomorphism. -/
   135	theorem of_iso (h : π.IsProjectiveWith L) {L' : X.Modules} (e : L ≅ L') :
   136	    π.IsProjectiveWith L' := by
   137	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp, ⟨eL⟩⟩ := h
   138	  exact ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp, ⟨e.symm ≪≫ eL⟩⟩
   139	
   140	/-- **Composition with a closed immersion**: if `π` is projective carrying
   141	`L` and `j` is a closed immersion into `X`, then `j ≫ π` is projective
   142	carrying `j^* L`. -/
   143	theorem comp_isClosedImmersion (h : π.IsProjectiveWith L) {Y : Scheme.{0}}
   144	    (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion j] :
   145	    (j ≫ π).IsProjectiveWith ((Scheme.Modules.pullback j).obj L) := by
   146	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
   147	  letI : Finite n := hn
   148	  haveI := hi
   149	  refine ⟨n, inferInstance, j ≫ i, inferInstance, by rw [Category.assoc, hcomp], ?_⟩
   150	  exact ⟨(Scheme.Modules.pullback j).mapIso e ≪≫
   151	    Scheme.pullbackTriangleIso (rfl : j ≫ i = j ≫ i)
   152	      (ProjectiveSpace.twistingSheaf n S 1)⟩
   153	
   154	/-- The comparison morphism from the base-changed total space into the
   155	base-changed projective space. -/
   156	private def baseChangeLift {S' : Scheme.{0}} (g : S' ⟶ S) {n : Type} [Finite n]
   157	    (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)) (hcomp : i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = π) :
   158	    pullback π g ⟶ ℙ(n; S') :=
   159	  (ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map n g).lift
   160	    (pullback.fst π g ≫ i) (pullback.snd π g)
   161	    (by rw [Category.assoc, hcomp, pullback.condition])
   162	
   163	/-- **Stability under base change**: if `π : X ⟶ S` is projective carrying
   164	`L` and `g : S' ⟶ S`, then the base change `X ×_S S' ⟶ S'` is projective
   165	carrying the pullback of `L`. -/
   166	theorem baseChange (h : π.IsProjectiveWith L) {S' : Scheme.{0}} (g : S' ⟶ S) :
   167	    (pullback.snd π g).IsProjectiveWith
   168	      ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π g)).obj L) := by
   169	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp, ⟨e⟩⟩ := h
   170	  letI : Finite n := hn
   171	  haveI := hi
   172	  refine ⟨n, inferInstance, baseChangeLift g i hcomp, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
   173	  · -- the comparison square exhibits the lift as the base change of `i`
   174	    have h1 : baseChangeLift g i hcomp ≫ (ℙ(n; S') ↘ S')
   175	        = pullback.snd π g := IsPullback.lift_snd _ _ _ _
   176	    have hsq : IsPullback (baseChangeLift g i hcomp) (pullback.fst π g)
   177	        (ProjectiveSpace.map n g) i := by
   178	      have hbig : IsPullback
   179	          (baseChangeLift g i hcomp ≫ (ℙ(n; S') ↘ S'))
   180	          (pullback.fst π g) g (i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S)) := by
   181	        rw [h1, hcomp]
   182	        exact (IsPullback.of_hasPullback π g).flip
   183	      exact IsPullback.of_right hbig
   184	        (IsPullback.lift_fst _ _ _ _)
   185	        (ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map n g).flip
   186	    exact MorphismProperty.of_isPullback hsq.flip hi
   187	  · exact IsPullback.lift_snd _ _ _ _
   188	  · refine ⟨(Scheme.Modules.pullback (pullback.fst π g)).mapIso e ≪≫
   189	      Scheme.pullbackTriangleIso (IsPullback.lift_fst _ _ _ _ :
   190	        baseChangeLift g i hcomp ≫ ProjectiveSpace.map n g
   191	          = pullback.fst π g ≫ i).symm
   192	        (ProjectiveSpace.twistingSheaf n S 1) ≪≫ ?_⟩
   193	    -- collapse `(lift ≫ map)^* O(1)` to `lift^* (map^* O(1))`, then use the
   194	    -- base-change isomorphism of the twist
   195	    exact (Scheme.pullbackTriangleIso
   196	        (rfl : baseChangeLift g i hcomp ≫ ProjectiveSpace.map n g
   197	          = _) (ProjectiveSpace.twistingSheaf n S 1)).symm ≪≫
   198	      (Scheme.Modules.pullback (baseChangeLift g i hcomp)).mapIso
   199	        (ProjectiveSpace.twistingSheafBaseChange n g 1)
   200	
   201	end Scheme.Hom.IsProjectiveWith
   202	
   203	namespace ProjectiveSpace
   204	
   205	/-- **The structural morphism of relative projective space is itself
   206	projective**, carrying the Serre twist `O(1)`: the canonical inhabitant of
   207	`IsProjectiveWith`, with the identity closed immersion.  This exhibits
   208	`ℙ(Fin (d+1); S) ↘ S` as the universal projective morphism and shows the
   209	predicate is non-vacuous. -/
   210	theorem isProjectiveWith_over (d : ℕ) (S : Scheme.{0}) :
   211	    (ℙ(Fin (d + 1); S) ↘ S).IsProjectiveWith (twistingSheaf (Fin (d + 1)) S 1) :=
   212	  ⟨Fin (d + 1), inferInstance, 𝟙 _, inferInstance, Category.id_comp _,
   213	    ⟨((Scheme.Modules.pullbackId _).app _).symm⟩⟩
   214	
   215	end ProjectiveSpace

   217	end AlgebraicGeometry

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.ProjectiveSpace

     8	/-!
     9	# Projective morphisms
    10	
    11	This file supplies the universe-polymorphic geometric core of projectivity that
    12	Mathlib v4.31 does not yet provide. A morphism is projective when it factors as
    13	a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional relative projective space.
    14	
    15	The line-bundle-carrying refinement used by the Quot construction remains in
    16	`Picard/ProjectiveMorphism.lean`; that refinement is universe-monomorphic because
    17	its Serre twist is built by the project-local sheaf gluing engine.
    18	-/
    19	
    20	open CategoryTheory Limits
    21	
    22	noncomputable section
    23	
    24	universe u
    25	
    26	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    27	
    28	/-- A morphism is projective if it admits a closed immersion into a
    29	finite-dimensional relative projective space over its target. -/
    30	def Scheme.Hom.IsProjective {X S : Scheme.{u}} (pi : X ⟶ S) : Prop :=
    31	  ∃ (n : Type u) (_ : Finite n) (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)),
    32	    IsClosedImmersion i ∧ i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi
    33	
    34	namespace Scheme.Hom.IsProjective
    35	
    36	variable {X S : Scheme.{u}} {pi : X ⟶ S}
    37	
    38	/-- Projective morphisms are proper. -/
    39	theorem isProper (h : pi.IsProjective) : IsProper pi := by
    40	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
    41	  letI : Finite n := hn
    42	  haveI := hi
    43	  rw [← hcomp]
    44	  infer_instance
    45	
    46	/-- Projective morphisms are locally of finite type. -/
    47	theorem locallyOfFiniteType (h : pi.IsProjective) : LocallyOfFiniteType pi :=
    48	  haveI := h.isProper
    49	  inferInstance
    50	
    51	/-- Projective morphisms are separated. -/
    52	theorem isSeparated (h : pi.IsProjective) : IsSeparated pi :=
    53	  haveI := h.isProper
    54	  inferInstance
    55	
    56	/-- Projective morphisms are universally closed. -/
    57	theorem universallyClosed (h : pi.IsProjective) : UniversallyClosed pi :=
    58	  haveI := h.isProper
    59	  inferInstance
    60	
    61	/-- A closed immersion into a projective scheme is projective. -/
    62	theorem comp_isClosedImmersion (h : pi.IsProjective) {Y : Scheme.{u}}
    63	    (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion j] : (j ≫ pi).IsProjective := by
    64	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
    65	  letI : Finite n := hn
    66	  haveI := hi
    67	  exact ⟨n, hn, j ≫ i, inferInstance, by rw [Category.assoc, hcomp]⟩
    68	
    69	/-- The comparison morphism from the base-changed source to the corresponding
    70	base change of its ambient projective space. -/
    71	private def baseChangeLift {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) {n : Type u}
    72	    (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)) (hcomp : i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi) :
    73	    pullback pi g ⟶ ℙ(n; S') :=
    74	  (ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map n g).lift
    75	    (pullback.fst pi g ≫ i) (pullback.snd pi g)
    76	    (by rw [Category.assoc, hcomp, pullback.condition])
    77	
    78	/-- Projective morphisms are stable under arbitrary base change. -/
    79	theorem baseChange (h : pi.IsProjective) {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) :
    80	    (pullback.snd pi g).IsProjective := by
    81	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
    82	  letI : Finite n := hn
    83	  haveI := hi
    84	  refine ⟨n, hn, baseChangeLift g i hcomp, ?_, ?_⟩
    85	  · have h1 : baseChangeLift g i hcomp ≫ (ℙ(n; S') ↘ S') =
    86	        pullback.snd pi g := IsPullback.lift_snd _ _ _ _
    87	    have hsq : IsPullback (baseChangeLift g i hcomp) (pullback.fst pi g)
    88	        (ProjectiveSpace.map n g) i := by
    89	      have hbig : IsPullback
    90	          (baseChangeLift g i hcomp ≫ (ℙ(n; S') ↘ S'))
    91	          (pullback.fst pi g) g (i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S)) := by
    92	        rw [h1, hcomp]
    93	        exact (IsPullback.of_hasPullback pi g).flip
    94	      exact IsPullback.of_right hbig
    95	        (IsPullback.lift_fst _ _ _ _)
    96	        (ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map n g).flip
    97	    exact MorphismProperty.of_isPullback hsq.flip hi
    98	  · exact IsPullback.lift_snd _ _ _ _
    99	
   100	end Scheme.Hom.IsProjective
   101	
   102	namespace ProjectiveSpace
   103	
   104	/-- The structural morphism of relative projective space is projective. -/

   125	
   126	The one step with mathematical content.  Everything else in this file is transport.
   127	-/
   128	
   129	section GradedAvoidance
   130	
   131	variable {σ : Type*} {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [SetLike σ A] [AddSubgroupClass σ A]
   132	variable (𝒜 : ℕ → σ) [GradedRing 𝒜]
   133	
   134	/-- **A finite `inf` of homogeneous ideals is homogeneous.** Bookkeeping for the
   135	avoidance argument, which needs `I ⊓ ⨅_{i ≠ j} p i` to be homogeneous in order to
   136	extract a homogeneous element from it. -/
   137	theorem Ideal.IsHomogeneous.finsetInf {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (p : ι → Ideal A)
   138	    (h : ∀ i ∈ s, (p i).IsHomogeneous 𝒜) : (s.inf p).IsHomogeneous 𝒜 := by
   139	  classical
   140	  induction s using Finset.induction with
   141	  | empty =>
   142	      rw [Finset.inf_empty]
   143	      exact fun _ _ _ => Submodule.mem_top
   144	  | insert a t _ IH =>
   145	      rw [Finset.inf_insert]
   146	      exact fun i x hx =>
   147	        ⟨h a (Finset.mem_insert_self a t) i hx.1,
   148	          IH (fun j hj => h j (Finset.mem_insert_of_mem hj)) i hx.2⟩
   149	
   150	/-- **Graded prime avoidance at a single relevant homogeneous prime.** If a
   151	homogeneous ideal `I` is not contained in a homogeneous prime `p`, and `p` does not
   152	contain the irrelevant ideal, then `I` has a homogeneous element of **strictly
   153	positive** degree outside `p`.
   154	
   155	Two separate uses of the grading, and it is worth naming both because the second is
   156	the one an ungraded intuition drops:
   157	
   158	* `I` homogeneous and `¬ I ≤ p` gives a homogeneous element of `I` outside `p` —
   159	  decompose a witness and note that if every component were in `p` so would the
   160	  witness be. Its degree is **not controlled** and may be `0`.
   161	* Relevance of `p` (`¬ 𝒜₊ ≤ p`) gives a homogeneous `g ∉ p` of positive degree, by
   162	  the same decomposition applied to a witness in the irrelevant ideal, whose
   163	  degree-`0` component is zero by definition.
   164	
   165	Then `f₀ * g` is homogeneous of degree `> 0`, lies in `I` (an ideal) and avoids `p`
   166	(a prime). Relevance is exactly what makes this possible: over a `p` containing
   167	`𝒜₊` — i.e. at a point *not* in `Proj` — every positive-degree homogeneous element
   168	lies in `p` and the conclusion is false. -/
   169	theorem exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_notMem
   170	    {I p : Ideal A} [hp : p.IsPrime] (hI : I.IsHomogeneous 𝒜)
   171	    (hrel : ¬ (HomogeneousIdeal.irrelevant 𝒜).toIdeal ≤ p) (hIp : ¬ I ≤ p) :
   172	    ∃ (m : ℕ) (f : A), 0 < m ∧ f ∈ 𝒜 m ∧ f ∈ I ∧ f ∉ p := by
   173	  classical
   174	  obtain ⟨n, f₀, hf₀deg, hf₀I, hf₀p⟩ : ∃ (n : ℕ) (f : A), f ∈ 𝒜 n ∧ f ∈ I ∧ f ∉ p := by
   175	    obtain ⟨x, hxI, hxp⟩ := SetLike.not_le_iff_exists.mp hIp
   176	    by_contra hcon
   177	    push Not at hcon
   178	    exact hxp (by
   179	      rw [← DirectSum.sum_support_decompose 𝒜 x]
   180	      refine Ideal.sum_mem _ fun i _ => ?_
   181	      by_contra h
   182	      exact h (hcon i _ (SetLike.coe_mem _) ((hI.mem_iff).mp hxI i)))
   183	  obtain ⟨m, g, hm, hgdeg, hgp⟩ : ∃ (m : ℕ) (g : A), 0 < m ∧ g ∈ 𝒜 m ∧ g ∉ p := by
   184	    obtain ⟨x, hxirr, hxp⟩ := SetLike.not_le_iff_exists.mp hrel
   185	    by_contra hcon
   186	    push Not at hcon
   187	    exact hxp (by
   188	      rw [← DirectSum.sum_support_decompose 𝒜 x]
   189	      refine Ideal.sum_mem _ fun i _ => ?_
   190	      rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos i with rfl | hi
   191	      · have hz : (DirectSum.decompose 𝒜 x 0 : A) = 0 := by
   192	          have := (HomogeneousIdeal.mem_irrelevant_iff 𝒜 x).mp hxirr
   193	          simpa [GradedRing.proj_apply] using this
   194	        simp [hz]
   195	      · exact hcon i _ hi (SetLike.coe_mem _))
   196	  exact ⟨n + m, f₀ * g, by omega, SetLike.mul_mem_graded hf₀deg hgdeg,
   197	    I.mul_mem_right _ hf₀I, fun h => (hp.mem_or_mem h).elim hf₀p hgp⟩
   198	
   199	/-- **Graded prime avoidance for an incomparable family** — the case with the
   200	construction in it.
   201	
   202	Given finitely many pairwise-incomparable relevant homogeneous primes `q ∈ T`, none
   203	containing the homogeneous ideal `I`, there is a **single** homogeneous element of
   204	`I` of **positive** degree outside every one of them.
   205	
   206	The classical product/sum trick, with the grading forcing one extra step:
   207	
   208	* Incomparability makes `I ⊓ ⨅_{q' ∈ T, q' ≠ q} q'` not contained in `q` — if it
   209	  were, primality would put one of the factors inside `q`. So
   210	  `exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_notMem` supplies, for each `q`, a homogeneous
   150	scheme-level form of the EGA II 4.5.4 orbit hypothesis.
   151	
   152	`SemilinearGalAction.OrbitsInAffineOpen` (`Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`) is
   153	stated *about an action*, so a consumer cannot discharge it before knowing which
   154	action it will face. This form is a property of the scheme alone, and §2 shows it
   155	implies the action form for **every** semilinear action of a finite Galois group.
   156	That is what lets the antecedent of §4 be stated without mentioning the Galois
   157	level, which is chosen inside the proof.
   158	
   159	True for quasi-projective schemes (finite point sets of a quasi-projective scheme
   160	lie in an affine open). Mathlib `v4.31` has no quasi-projectivity vocabulary at
   161	this pin, which is why the hypothesis is carried in this elementary form rather
   162	than derived. -/
   163	def FiniteInAffine (X : Scheme.{u}) : Prop :=
   164	  ∀ s : Set X, s.Finite → ∃ U : X.affineOpens, s ⊆ U.1
   165	
   166	/-- **The pointed Picard theorem**: FGA/Kleiman representability of the relative
   167	Picard functor, for curves that *have* a rational point, uniformly in the base
   168	field, together with quasi-projectivity of the representing scheme.
   169	
   170	This is the campaign's target, written as a closed proposition. Three things about
   171	its shape are deliberate, and a fourth is deliberately **absent**.
   172	
   173	* It quantifies over **all** base fields `K`, not just over `k`. That is
   174	  essential and it is not a strengthening in any useful sense: §4 applies it at a
   175	  finite Galois extension of `k` chosen by the curve, so a version fixed at `k`
   176	  would not compose. Every formalisation route to FGA representability is uniform
   177	  in the base field anyway.
   178	* It is about `picSharp`, the **unsheafified** relative Picard functor — the object
   179	  the Milne–Kollár modules target (`I-0907`). No étale-sheafified representability
   180	  statement is needed on top of it; §3 of `Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean` supplies
   181	  the transport for free.
   182	* `FiniteInAffine X.left` is bundled rather than carried separately so that the
   183	  results below have **one** antecedent. The *property* is perfectly stateable
   184	  outside it — `HasGoodGaloisLevel` in §5 does exactly that, and §2 takes it as a
   185	  free-standing hypothesis. What cannot be stated outside is the **witness**: no
   186	  separate binder can name the scheme the antecedent itself produces. (An earlier
   187	  revision of this bullet said the property "cannot be stated outside it", which
   188	  two declarations in this same file refute.)
   189	* **`IsSeparated X.hom` is NOT a conjunct**, and carrying it would have
   190	  misreported the price of the reduction. It is *free* from the resulting `picEt`
   191	  representation by `isSeparated_of_representableBy_picEt`
   192	  (`Picard/PicEtSeparated.lean`) — Yoneda transports the `CommGrpCat`-valued
   193	  functor's group structure onto any representing scheme, and a group scheme over
   194	  a field is separated. That file's
   195	  `picEtClauseOne_of_picSharp_representableBy_locallyOfFiniteType` already says
   196	  in its own docstring that the form to hand the campaign asks "nothing about
   197	  separatedness". A first revision of this file bundled it anyway; a
   198	  fresh-context audit reproved every result with the conjunct deleted, so it is
   199	  deleted. The seam's clause (1) still *concludes* separatedness — it is
   200	  discharged, not dropped. -/
   201	def PointedPicSharpRep : Prop :=
   202	  ∀ {K : Type u} [Field K] (E : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))),
   203	    ∀ [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 E.hom] [IsProper E.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral E.hom],
   204	      Scheme.HasRationalPoint E →
   205	      ∃ X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)),
   206	        Nonempty ((PicScheme.picSharp E).RepresentableBy X) ∧
   207	          LocallyOfFiniteType X.hom ∧ FiniteInAffine X.left
   208	
   209	/-! ## §2. The scheme-level hypothesis implies the action-level one -/
   210	
   211	/-- **`FiniteInAffine` discharges `OrbitsInAffineOpen`, for every semilinear
   212	action of a finite Galois group.**
   213	
   214	The orbit of a point is the range of a map indexed by `L ≃ₐ[K] L`, which is finite
   215	because `L/K` is finite Galois (`Finite (L ≃ₐ[K] L)` by synthesis), so it is a
   216	finite subset and the hypothesis applies directly.
   217	
   218	Note where the finiteness of the group is consumed: only here. The quotient
   219	machinery downstream binds `[FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]` for its own
   220	reasons. -/
   221	theorem orbitsInAffineOpen_of_finiteInAffine
   222	    {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
   223	    [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
   224	    {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
   225	    (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) (h : FiniteInAffine X) :
   226	    ρ.OrbitsInAffineOpen where
   227	  exists_affineOpen x := by
   228	    obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ :=
   229	      h (Set.range fun γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L => (ρ.act γ).hom.base x) (Set.finite_range _)
   230	    exact ⟨U, fun γ => hU ⟨γ, rfl⟩⟩
   231

   233	
   234	Both directions are recorded as declarations rather than as docstring sentences,
   235	per `I-0838`: a hypothesis whose satisfiability is unmeasured is how a vacuous
   645	    Function.Bijective fun p : (Σ d : ℕ, (DivFunctorDeg C.hom d).obj T) =>

   650	/-! ## §7. A2 — the degree-refined Abel map -/
   651	
   652	namespace PicScheme
   653	
   654	variable {k : Type u} [Field k]
   655	
   656	/-- The degree-`d` relative-divisor functor of the AJC curve,
   657	`Div^d_{C/k} := DivFunctorDeg C.hom d` — the A.2.c-side avatar of the general
   658	degree slice, mirroring `divFunctor C = DivFunctor C.hom`
   659	(`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`). -/
   660	noncomputable def divFunctorDeg (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (d : ℕ) :
   661	    (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u + 1) :=
   662	  DivFunctorDeg C.hom d

   665	(Kleiman §3 Def. `dfn:Abel`, restricted to the degree-`d` slice): the
   666	composite of the degree-`d` inclusion with the substantive Abel map
   667	`abelMapWitness C`, so on points
   668	
   669	  `[D] ↦ [O(D)] = [I_D⁻¹] = -[ker q]`  (defining property `abelDeg_app_mk`).
   670	
   671	Sign convention (audit item 7-half): the divisor class maps to the **negative**
   672	of the ideal-sheaf class; the fibre-degree ledger for the ideal side is
   673	`DivFamily.fiberDeg_eq_finrank_fiber_cokernel` ("`ker q` has fibre degree
   674	`−d`" in the rank vocabulary — module docstring audit).  The target is
   675	deliberately the full `picSharp C`: carving out the degree-`d` Picard
   676	subfunctor `picSharpDeg C d` is campaign milestone B4, and refactoring
   677	`abelDeg` to corestrict onto it is part of that milestone, not this one. -/
   678	noncomputable def abelDeg (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   679	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] (d : ℕ) :
   680	    divFunctorDeg C d ⟶ picSharp C :=
   681	  divFunctorDegι C.hom d ≫ abelMapWitness C
   682	
   683	/-- **Defining property of the degree-refined Abel map** (Kleiman §3
   684	Def. `dfn:Abel`): on the class of a degree-`d` divisor family `⟨F, q⟩` it
   685	returns `[O(D)] = [I_D⁻¹]`, the additive inverse of the class of the ideal
   686	sheaf `I_D = ker q` — the `[D] ↦ -[ker q]` sign convention, verbatim
   687	compatible with `abelMap_app_mk` through the inclusion. -/
   688	theorem abelDeg_app_mk (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   689	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] (d : ℕ)
   690	    (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) (x : DivFamily C.hom T.unop)
   691	    (hx : DivFamily.ClassHasFiberDeg d
   692	      (Quotient.mk (DivFamily.setoid C.hom T.unop) x)) :
   693	    (abelDeg C d).app T ⟨Quotient.mk (DivFamily.setoid C.hom T.unop) x, hx⟩ =
   694	      - Quotient.mk (PicSharp.relPicSetoid C.hom T.unop.hom)
   695	        (⟨kernel x.q, x.kerLocallyTrivial⟩ :
   696	          LineBundle.OnProduct C.hom T.unop.hom) :=
   697	  rfl

   700	degree-`d` inclusion — definitional, recorded for the blueprint. -/

   702	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] (d : ℕ) :
   703	    abelDeg C d = divFunctorDegι C.hom d ≫ abelMapWitness C :=

/-!
# The Quot functor and the relative Grassmannian functor

This file constructs the two headline *definitions* of the A.2.b Quot-scheme
chapter (`blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_QuotScheme.tex`):

* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.QuotFunctor` (`def:quot_functor`) — the Quot
  functor `Quot^{Φ,L}_{E/X/S} : (Sch/S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u+1)` of `T`-flat, finitely
  presented quotients `q : E_T ↠ F` on `X_T = X ×_S T` with proper support
  and fibrewise Hilbert polynomial `Φ`, modulo `ker q = ker q'`;
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Grassmannian` (`def:grassmannian_scheme`) — the
  relative Grassmannian functor `Grass(V, d) : (Sch/S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (u+1)` of
  rank-`d` locally free quotients of `V_T` on `T`.

Universe note: the value category is `Type (u+1)`, not `Type u` — a sheaf of
modules on a scheme in `Scheme.{u}` is a large object, so the quotient sets
live one universe up.  The same shift occurs for the absolute Grassmannian
functor (`AlgebraicGeometry.Grassmannian.functor`, `GrassmannianQuot.lean`)
and for `picSharp` (`FGAPicRepresentability.lean`); `Functor.RepresentableBy`
is universe-polymorphic, so the representability statements are unaffected.
